title: rolling-window-shotforge-scratch
content:
Notes: rolling-window-shotforge (one-off scratch)

Goal:
- Explore a lightweight rolling-window few-shot strategy to keep exemplar relevance while capping token cost.
- Blend short-term session examples with a small stable archetype bank.
- Study failure modes when exemplar drift + long context cause hallucination.

Motivation / hypothesis:
- For chat assistants we can't pass entire history. A full-memory window is expensive and often redundant.
- If we keep a small ephemeral window (last 2-4 user turns) + 3 archetypes chosen by a cheap similarity measure, we get better recency without blowing token budget.
- Problem: exemplar overlap and contradictory instructions cause output flip-flops. Need heuristics for replacement and precedence.

Quick architecture sketch (informal):
- Input: user turn + metadata (intent tag if available)
- Retriever: cosine on compressed embeddings (32-d PCA from 1536) against archetype bank (<= 200 entries) cheap L2 fallback.
- Rolling window: keep last 3 user-assistant pairs; these are sent as "SESSION_EXEMPLARS" in order newest->oldest.
- Archetype selection: top-3 similar archetypes minus any that overlap in intent label with session exemplars. If overlap, prefer diverse archetype by cosine distance threshold.
- Ordering: put archetypes after session exemplars, but mark archetype boundaries with explicit header token like "--EXEMPLAR--" to reduce blending.
- Token cap: max 1400 tokens for exemplars. Truncate oldest archetype first.

Experiment plan (small-scale):
1) Create 120 archetypes from internal chat logs (support + product prompts) — compress to vector store.
2) Build 3 workloads: 
   a) task-oriented Q&A (support),
   b) open-ended writing assist (marketing copy),
   c) instruction-following (developer docs).
3) For each workload run these policies: None (baseline), Full history (if available), Rolling-window-only (3 pairs), Rolling-window + archetypes (top-3), Static-template-only (3 fixed exemplars).
4) Metrics: exact-match (where applicable), instruction-fidelity score (human label 0-3), token-cost per response, latency delta.

Sample few-shot template (rough):
---SYSTEM: You are an assistant that answers succinctly and cites short action steps when applicable.---
{SESSION_EXEMPLARS}
--EXEMPLAR--
User: I need a short onboarding email for a new feature called "SmartFilters" targeted at SMEs.
Assistant: Subject: SmartFilters — Make discovery faster
Steps: 1) quick benefit 2) 2-line how-to 3) CTA

User: Create the email now.
Assistant: [expected concise output]

Session exemplar formatting notes (trial variations):
- Variant A: include explicit label "Intent:" on exemplar header. Seems to help for task routing but increases token use.
- Variant B: include "Desired-Tone:" metadata per exemplar (short token overhead) — seems to reduce tone drift in open-ended tasks.

Failure cases observed (early manual probes):
- Contradictory exemplars -> assistant blends contradictory instructions (e.g., exemplar says "always be formal" + another says "casual"). Need precedence rule: session exemplars > archetypes > static templates.
- Overfitting to archetype phrasing: assistant copies phrasing templates too literally. Mitigation: mask named entities in archetypes, or replace with placeholders (ENTITY_1) to encourage synthesis.
- Relevance drop: top-k similarity picks obvious technical matches but they are stale (old product names). Need product-name blacklist or recency boost.

Edge heuristics to implement (checklist):
- [ ] Preprocess archetypes: de-dup at 0.85 cosine, remove PII, anonymize company names.
- [ ] Add "recency score" for archetypes from last 18 months.
- [ ] Build quick intent classifier (tiny transformer or logistic over bag-of-words) to tag session intent cheaply.
- [ ] Prepend clear precedence comment in prompt: "When exemplars disagree follow the newest session exemplar." (test whether explicit instruction helps).

Token-budget experiments (notes):
- Target exemplar budget = 1200 tokens. With average archetype ~180 tokens, top-3 + window (3 pairs) often hits ~1000-1300. Need dynamic trimming: if window+top3 > cap then truncate archetypes first.
- Try alternative: keep one long archetype + two micro-exemplars (short 40-token). Compare fidelity.

Shot examples to test (concrete):
- Support: user reports an error and mentions stack trace fragment. See whether exemplar bank with similar error patterns helps exact diagnosis.
- Marketing: user asks for blog intro about X; archetype bank should include winning headlines; watch for plagiarism risk.
- Code: user asks to refactor small function; exemplars should be small code examples not full files. Test with code-runner unit checks.

Human evaluation rubric (quick draft):
- 0: Wrong/unsafe/irrelevant
- 1: On-topic but misses core ask or wrong steps
- 2: Satisfies ask with minor style issues
- 3: High-quality, actionable, succinct

Open questions / unknowns (notes-to-self):
- How much does ordering archetypes by similarity vs by recency matter? Test both.
- Does explicit separator token reduce hallucination or increase brittle boundary artifacts? A/B.
- Should we use model-side retrieval context windowing (store compressed cache on host) vs client-side assembly? Latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Privacy: archetypes might leak customer wording. Need opt-out and L0 redaction.

Quick TODOs for next pairing session with Priya:
- Generate 120 archetypes and run de-dupe. (assign: Priya)
- Prototype small retriever + PCA compressor (assign: me)
- Create 60 human eval pairs across 3 workloads (assign: Liam)

Scratch examples (live tinkering):
- Prompt A (short): "You are a support assistant. Given the user description produce 3 diagnostic steps and one probable cause"
- Prompt B (with exemplars): [session exemplar block]
